saints.name: St. Stephen
saints.title: The First Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The first of the seven deacons and the first martyr of the Church, who saw heaven open as he was stoned…
biography: Stephen — his Greek name means a crown — stands first among the seven deacons chosen to serve the poor of Jerusalem. Full of faith and the Holy Spirit, he worked wonders and disputed with the synagogues of the Libertines, Cyrenians, Alexandrians, Cilicians, and Asians, who could not withstand his wisdom (Acts 6).

Accused by hired witnesses of blasphemy against Moses and the Temple, he stood before the Sanhedrin, his face shining as an angel's. His defence closed in a cry: 'Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.'

Cast out of the city, he was stoned, the witnesses laying their garments at the feet of young Saul. Kneeling, he prayed, 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit,' and, 'Lord, lay not this sin to their charge'; and so fell asleep, about the year 34.

Devout men buried him with great mourning. In 415 his tomb was revealed to the priest Lucian at Caphar Gamala, and the relics were enshrined in the basilica built by the Empress Eudocia. First of the deacons, he is patron of deacons; slain by stones, of stonemasons, and invoked against pains of the head.
saints.knownFor: The Church's first martyr; deacon of Jerusalem.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 26 December
